newsitem.title: USA: Phillips' has significant North Sea find.
newsitem.headline: Phillips' has significant North Sea find.

text.p: BARTLESVILLE, Okla., Feb 20 (Reuter) Phillips Petroleum Co said Thursday a significant discovery has been made in Block 30/2c in the U.K.'s central North Sea.

The Jade accumulation is located 12 miles north of the Phillips-operated Judy field. It is a separate structure from all other fields in the area, Phillips said. The company is the operator with a 32.5 percent interest. Other owners are BG Plc, 35 percent; Texaco Inc, 15.4 percent; Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap A/S's Statoil (UK) Ltd., 10 percent; and OMV AG, 7.1 percent.

Phillips said it completed drilling the discovery well, 30/2c-3, in March 1996; but suspended the well without testing due to rig-time constraints. The well encountered a hydrocarbon column of more than 1,250 feet with no water contact. In anticipation of possible field development, Phillips said, it installed a nine-slot spacer frame on the seabed in November 1996.

It then drilled the 30/2c-4 appraisal well from the spacer frame to a depth of 16,867 feet, encountering a hydrocarbon column more than 1,300 feet thick with no water contact, confirming and extending the results of the discovery well.

Phillips said it tested two intervals in the appraisal well. The lower interval flowed at a stabilized rate of 33 million cubic feet of natural gas and 6,000 barrels of 47 degree condensate per day on a 48/64-inch choke. The upper interval flowed at 58 million cubic feet of natural gas and 3,700 barrels of condensate per day on a 48/64-inch choke.

"The Jade discovery is a significant find for Phillips and its co-venturers," said Knut Am, senior vice president, exploration and production. "We will continue to evaluate ... the potential commerciality of the Jade discovery, while we press forward with various development schemes."
Both the discovery well and the appraisal well are high-pressure, high-temperature wells and have been suspended for re-entry and completion during development.
In order to reduce time to first production, development conceptual studies have been progressing in parallel with appraisal drilling, Phillips said.

Studies completed to date indicate production could start as early as the fourth quarter of 1998. Phillips said it will discuss various development options with the Department of Trade and Industry later this year.

The Jade accumulation is situated in a different license block from those in which the Judy/Joanne fields are located, the company pointed out. Thus it is not directly connected with the disputes and litigation currently under way involving the Judy/Joanne gas sales contracts.
